historical_growth.growth_rate_source: H1-2026 run-rate (+8.1% revenue) blended across segments: commercial management (~38% of revenue) growing 13-15%, property management (~60%) growing 1-3%. Historical CAGRs are inflated by the FY2021-23 acquisition and post-IPO ramp and are not forward proxies.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.7% / 4.4%) diverges >30% from revenue (14.5% / 21.6%) and EPS (21.6% / 29.1%) because the company pays out 100% of core net profit (RMB4.88bn in FY2025, RMB0.977/share interim in 2026) and the FY2020 base includes the IPO proceeds. Equity growth is therefore not a usable growth proxy here; growth is selected from the segment run-rate instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest income; SBC is zero). The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (40.2%) exceeds the reported (29.8%) because interest income fell from RMB424.6m (FY2022) to RMB161.5m (FY2025) as cash moved into time deposits and FVTPL products whose returns are not in OCF - the opposite of the SBC-outgrowing-cash warning. FY2025 revenue growth is +5.1% on the restated FY2024 base (17,154.4), +5.7% on the as-first-reported CSV figure (17,042.7).

scenario_narratives.base: China consumption grows at low-to-mid single digits in nominal terms; CR Land keeps delivering 10-14 new Mixc/Mixc One malls a year and the group adds a handful of third-party malls, so commercial-management revenue compounds at low-double-digits while shopping-mall retail sales (RMB266bn in 2025, +~15%) outgrow the market. Property management (60% of revenue) grows 1-3%: new state-owned-enterprise and urban-space contracts offset deliberate exits from low-margin third-party residential projects (the Nantong/Xiamen withdrawals). Mix shift lifts post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin from 29.4% to ~31.5% over four years, then it plateaus. The 100% payout continues; the RMB15bn liquid pile is returned over time rather than deployed into acquisitions at poor returns. Revenue growth decays from 7.5% to 3%, terminal 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Domestic-demand stimulus and the 'Property Service Improvement Initiative' in the 15th Five-Year Plan lift mall retail sales and tenant sales-linked fees; third-party mall wins (12 new contracts in 2025) accelerate so commercial management grows mid-teens for several years, office leasing fills on the financial-institution strategic projects, and the membership/ecosystem business (CR Life Club) scales at 30-37% gross margin. Property-management margins recover as the mix tilts toward SOE and urban-space contracts and AI-driven cost control bites. EBITDA margin reaches 34%; growth starts at 10% and decays to 4%; terminal 3.0%, cap 20x reflecting a scarce SOE-backed consumer franchise.
scenario_narratives.bear: A prolonged China property and consumption downturn: CR Land slows mall completions, same-mall retail sales stall and rent concessions compress the 76% mall gross margin; property-management fees face local price caps and collection rates fall, with developer and owner receivables (RMB3.0bn and growing ~15%/yr against +5% revenue) needing larger impairments - working capital capture -10% of revenue growth. The subleasing portfolio's fixed lease cost rises as a share of revenue. Growth drops to 1-2%, EBITDA margin compresses to 27%, cash tax rises with less preferential-rate income. Terminal 2.0% and a 15x cap because a slow-growing, regulated service business with parent-pipeline dependence does not command a premium multiple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on an asset-light, zero-debt services business whose economics are a blend of a high-margin, growing shopping-mall operator and a low-margin, mature property manager. Flows are stripped of investment income and non-cash revaluation gains; the RMB17bn of cash, deposits and principal-protected products is added back at fair value, less the dividend already declared against it. Leases on sub-let malls are an operating cost (treatment B), not debt. The valuation is reported in HKD at the 2026-10-16 CNY/HKD rate so it is comparable to the HKEX price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Parent dependence: most new malls and much of the office/PM pipeline come from CR Land; a slowdown in CR Land completions or a change in related-party terms moves the growth path directly.

Regulatory pricing of residential property-management fees and the collectability of developer/owner receivables (RMB3.0bn at Jun-2026, growing ~15%/yr) - the bear case charges this through margin and working capital.

Capital allocation of the RMB15bn liquid pile: common-control acquisitions from the parent (RMB121m in FY2025) and the proposed consumer fund could redeploy cash at below-WACC returns; the model credits it at face value.
FX: value is built in CNY and translated at 1.1729 CNY/HKD; a 5% RMB depreciation against HKD is a ~5% lower HKD value with no change in the business.
Mall gross margin (75.9%) and the sub-leasing portfolio are sensitive to retail-sales-linked fees; a consumption downturn hits the highest-margin 26% of revenue first.
Terminal assumptions: ~55-65% of value is terminal at a 9.5% CNY discount rate; +/-1pp on WACC or terminal growth moves the base IV by roughly 10-15% (see sensitivity grid).

inputs.share_count_basis: 2,282,500,000 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1-2026 interim report); basic EPS equals diluted EPS in every period since listing, so there are no dilutive instruments. Held flat: SBC is zero and there is no non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: no share option, share award or other equity-settled scheme in operation; the only 'share schemes' mention is a board-committee remit. Cash flow reconciliation carries no share-based payment add-back. Treated as genuinely zero (SBC-zero market), rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1729 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-16T07:40Z. Parity check: the company converted the 2026 interim dividend of RMB0.586 to HK$0.677 (1.155) and the 2025 final of RMB0.509 to HK$0.585 (1.149) at their declaration dates, so the direction (multiply CNY values by ~1.15-1.17 to get HKD) is confirmed. No dual listing exists for a price parity check.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T06:32:46Z (regular HKEX afternoon session; not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are CNY, so the rate is built in CNY: 10y China Government Bond ~1.8%, China equity risk premium ~6.5% at beta ~1.0, plus ~1.2pp for HK-listed China-services governance/liquidity risk = ~9.5% cost of equity. No interest-bearing debt (bank borrowings zero since FY2022), so WACC = cost of equity = 9.5%. Same rate in all three scenarios; operating, regulatory and developer-receivable risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. The group leases shopping malls and sub-leases units to tenants; the leased assets sit in investment properties at fair value (RMB4,795m at 30 Jun 2026) and the liabilities (RMB2,188m) are the matching obligation. The full lease payment (principal + interest, RMB249.0m in FY2025 = 1.38% of revenue, FY2024 RMB263.7m) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt and investment properties are EXCLUDED from the bridge. The ebitda_margin_path is therefore the post-IFRS-16 EBITDA (FY2025 29.4%) and da_pct is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation. Investment-property revaluation gains (RMB263.6m FY2025, RMB79.8m H1-2026) are non-cash and excluded from the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Minority interests (RMB242m book at 30 Jun 2026) take ~2.8% of group profit (RMB114.7m of RMB4,083.7m in FY2025), which at book materially understates their claim. Charged once by folding the leakage into cash_tax_rate_path: ~25-26% cash tax on EBIT plus ~2pp NCI leakage = 27.5% base. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (CNY-built WACC, lease treatment B, NCI folded into tax, SBC-zero, excluded-income/matching-asset rule). Routing: operating company (asset-light property management + shopping-mall/office commercial operations, spun out of CR Land in Dec 2020), not a developer, REIT or holdco. FY0 EBITDA anchor: gross profit 6,405.6 - marketing 295.6 - admin 1,062.7 - other expenses 187.8 (impairments of developer/other receivables, treated as a recurring cost) + government grants 54.4 + other operating income 50.6 = EBIT-before-D&A-addback 4,964.5; + D&A 338.7 (PPE 127.5, ROU 55.3, intangibles 155.9) = 5,303 = 29.4% of revenue; less lease payments 249.0 = 28.0% owner EBITDA (FY2024 restated: 25.7%). Interest income (RMB161.5m) and FVTPL gains (RMB170.7m) are stripped from the flows and their source assets are added in the bridge at 30 Jun 2026 fair value. da_pct 0.75% is PPE depreciation plus non-acquisition software amortisation; customer-relationship amortisation (bulk of the 155.9 intangibles charge) is acquisition accounting, non-deductible and running off, so it earns no tax shield here. Cash tax: FY2025 tax paid RMB1,368.9m (28.7% of post-lease EBIT, elevated vs the 23.7% P&L rate by timing and dividend withholding tax on the 100% payout); FY2024 20.0%; two-year average ~25%; base 27.5% includes ~2pp NCI leakage. NOPAT tie-out: FY0 EBIT 4,771 x (1-0.275) = 3,459 attributable vs core net profit 3,950 less post-tax investment income (~249) less the customer-relationship amortisation core NP adds back (~117) = 3,584; the 3.5% gap is the cash-vs-effective tax rate. Working capital was net -37 in FY2025 and +477 in FY2024 (receivables growing ~15%/yr against +5% revenue, offset by other payables); base capture 0. Dividend policy: 100% of core net profit paid out in FY2025 and H1-2026 (RMB0.977/share interim incl. special), so retained equity is flat and the equity CAGR is not a growth proxy. Buybacks: none ever; the flat count is a convention the company has not had to pay for, but with zero SBC there is nothing to fund. The FY2024 column in the CSV is as first reported (17,042.7); the FY2025 annual restated it to 17,154.4 for common-control acquisitions (Zhengzhou Kanglong, CR Networks SZ, China Net Data GZ) - FY2025 growth is +5.1% on the restated basis, used here. Guidance: management gives no numeric guidance; H1-2026 revenue +8.1%, core net profit +10.8%, shopping malls +15.2%, offices +8.6%, property management ~+3%, ecosystem +88%.

net_cash_composition_30jun2026.note: Interest-bearing borrowings have been zero since FY2022. The 2025 final + special dividend (RMB0.85/share, RMB1,940.1m) was approved at the June 2026 AGM, sat in other payables at 30 June and was paid 30 July 2026, so it is deducted. The 2026 interim + special interim (RMB0.977/share, ~RMB2,230m, paid ~26 Oct 2026) was declared after the balance date and is funded from H2 cash generation not in this balance sheet; the price is ex both.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 7.5% vs H1 +8.1% (H2 comps tougher as FY2025 H2 carried the common-control acquisitions). Decelerates 0.5pp/yr as the CR Land mall pipeline (14 openings in 2025, 135 malls in operation) matures and property management stays low-single-digit.
base.margin_rationale: Post-IFRS-16 EBITDA 29.4% in FY2025 (27.2% FY2024). Mix shift toward malls (76-79% gross margin, growing ~15%) against property management (18%, growing ~3%) adds ~0.5pp/yr for four years, then plateaus at 31.5% as mall gross margin expansion runs out and PM pricing stays regulated.
base.tax_rationale: ~25.5% cash tax on EBIT (25% statutory, 15% on a few preferential subsidiaries, plus 5% dividend withholding on the 100% payout) + ~2pp NCI leakage.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the growth engine depends on a single parent's (CR Land) development pipeline, property-management pricing is regulated at the local-government level, and receivables are growing three times faster than revenue - these are correlated China-property-cycle risks, not independent operating ones. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several things at once: a durable consumption recovery, continued third-party mall wins, and PM margin repair. Base 50%: the business is net cash with no debt, 100% payout, and a decade of disclosed mall-opening pipeline, so the central case is well anchored.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
